message.content: {"basis": "The map legend (chart_1, lower right) is a vertical color scale where pale yellow at the top is labeled “High” with a tick of 100, and dark burgundy/maroon at the bottom is labeled “Low” with a tick of 0. The state polygon labeled “WV” (chart_1, central Appalachian area) is filled with the same pale-yellow color as the top/High end of the legend, placing its incidence at or near the 100 mark. The state polygon labeled “UT” (chart_1, southwestern area) is filled with the dark-burgundy/maroon color at the bottom/Low end of the legend, placing its incidence at or near 0. The southeastern polygon corresponding to Alabama is filled gray, a color not present on the legend gradient, and it lacks a visible “AL” inscription; gray is used elsewhere (e.g., CA, AK) to denote unmapped/no-value states, so it is not eligible to exceed a mapped state. Comparing the eligible mapped options, WV’s High/100 color is strictly greater than UT’s Low/0 color, so WV has the highest incidence among the offered records and should be routed to the highest-incidence priority follow-up workflow.", "option_label": "Open West Virginia (WV) incidence detail for priority follow-up"}
